::: {.callout-important}
San Francisco is a prominent center of Autonomous Vehicle (AV) activity. Data describing AV activity in San Francisco, however, is spread across multiple sources, redacted from public reports, collected with insufficient detail, or in some cases not collected at all. 
:::

## Data Sources
The data used in the AV Resource Portal is from public versions of data released by the California Department of Motor Vehicles (California DMV), California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC), and National Highway Transportation Safety Administration (NHTSA).

### National Highway Transportation Safety Administration
NHTSA's [Standing General Order (SGO)](https://www.nhtsa.gov/sites/nhtsa.gov/files/2025-04/third-amended-SGO-2021-01_2025.pdf) is the most comprehensive source of AV collision data in the United States.  The third amendment to the SGO changed the data schema and the requirements specifying which events must be reported, but the new version is largely compatible with the legacy data.

The SGO data is typically updated monthly.  Some data in the public version is truncated or redacted, including:

- Vehicle identifiers: `VIN`, `Serial Number`
- Location information: `Latitude`, `Longitude`, `Address`, `Zip Code`
- Other: `Narrative`, `Within ODD?`

The SGO data may contain multiple records for each individual incident, as companies file updated reports with NHTSA.  If you are working with this, take care to use the newest version of each incident record, identified by `Same Incident ID`.

[source](https://www.nhtsa.gov/laws-regulations/standing-general-order-crash-reporting)

### California Department of Motor Vehicles 
The DMV approved [new regulations](https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/autonomous-vehicles/california-autonomous-vehicle-regulations/) on [April 28, 2026](https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/news-and-media/new-autonomous-vehicle-regulations-strengthen-oversight-and-enforcement-authorize-trucks-and-transit/), which expand data reporting to include new types of data and, importantly, require companies with deployment permits to report data. Previous regulations only required companies with testing permits to report data. The first quarterly reports under the new regulations will cover the period July 1, 2026 - September 30, 2026. It is not clear if or when quarterly report data will be made available to the public.

Data under the previous rules was reported annually covering a period of December - November, and typically released the following February.  The reporting cadence results in a long lag in data availability and the data reporting period inhibits interoperability with other data sources. 

VMT data is reported without geographic detail, and prior to new regulations was not reported in deployment at all.  

[source](https://dmvpublicaffairs.wetransfer.com/downloads/e6a196103b7a16801d4acd452cf7e35c20260220222733/70cc0b?t_lsid=e71827f1-358f-4135-a906-b9f4223c5633&t_network=link&t_rid=YXV0aDB8VHJhbnNmZXJ8cGg2MjFxMHI5bmc=&t_s=download_link&t_ts=1771626453)

### California Public Utilities Commission
The CPUC collects rudimentary data for companies operating with pilot permits, and much more extensive data for companies operating under deployment permits.  

Pilot permittees over 300 trips per quarter are subject to deployment reporting requirements. Pilot data is submitted in different file formats and data schemas by different companies, making it very difficult to use.  

Deployment data is composed of 9 individual reports filed quarterly. These reports are much more comprehensive and detailed than pilot reports, but they are heavily redacted.  

[source](https://www.cpuc.ca.gov/regulatory-services/licensing/transportation-licensing-and-analysis-branch/autonomous-vehicle-programs/quarterly-reporting)

## Interoperability and Challenges
The [vehicles and people](./vehicles_and_people.html) and [safety](./safety.html) pages use callout boxes to identify how data limitations affect the information presented.  

Some of the key issues are:

- The CPUC's quarterly pilot reports are structured differently and are incompatible with the quarterly deployment reports
- CPUC and DMV reports can only be aligned at the statewide, monthly level
- DMV reports are only available through November 2025
- Neither the CPUC nor DMV reports can be aligned with NHTSA data for safety analysis
